display: John Henry Holliday was born on August 14, 1851, in Griffin, Georgia.
In 1866 Holliday's mother died of tuberculosis.
He enrolled at the Pennsylvania College of Dental Surgery in 1870 and graduated in 1872, then practiced dentistry in Atlanta before opening his own practice in Griffin.

Shortly after beginning his career as a dentist in Atlanta he developed a bad cough; doctors diagnosed tuberculosis and advised a move to a more arid climate. He developed chronic pulmonary tuberculosis.
He was diagnosed with tuberculosis in 1873 and moved west for a healthier, drier climate, arriving in Dallas, Texas, in September 1873.
He made his living at the card tables, aggravating his tuberculosis with heavy drinking and late nights.
He died of tuberculosis in its final stages on November 8, 1887, in Glenwood Springs, Colorado, at the age of 36.
Pulmonary tuberculosis, right upper lobe cavitary, sputum smear-positive, confirmed by nucleic acid amplification without rifampin resistance
